title: Government’s Response to Recommendations from Institute of Policy Studies Report on Stay-at-home Fathers
what_it_is: Government’s Response to Recommendations from Institute of Policy Studies Report on Stay-at-home Fathers

sections.label: Father involvement and child outcomes
sections.summary: International studies show that greater father involvement leads to better physical, cognitive and emotional developmental outcomes for children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: International studies have shown that when fathers are more involved, their children have better physical, cognitive and emotional developmental outcomes.

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up and support
sections.summary: Paternity and shared parental leave were increased, take-up rates rose, and the priority is encouraging more fathers to take leave before further enhancements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In 2017, we increased paternity leave and shared parental leave to two and four weeks respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Today, fathers can tap on eight weeks of leave in their child's first year, almost double the amount compared to five years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We are glad to see that more fathers are using their paternity leave, with take-up rates increasing from 25% in 2013 to 53% for recent cohorts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Our priority should, therefore, be to encourage and enable more fathers to take their paternity leave before considering further enhancements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to identify ways to better support parents in managing their work and family responsibilities, such as by promoting the adoption of flexible work arrangements, and working with employers and community partners to strengthen attitudes and norms in support of fatherhood.

sections.label: Workplace norms and preschool alternatives
sections.summary: Groups said workplace norms must be addressed and alternatives made available to families, with more done on preschool.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What the groups have told us very clearly is that in addition to all the things that we are doing on parental leave, it is also important to address workplace norms, and actually, more importantly, we have to make alternatives available to the families.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The alternative that is available in today's context of nuclear families, smaller families and also because grandparents are working, is, "Please do more with regard to preschool".
